summary: A BBC News track-by-track guide to Taylor Swift's 1989, released in a re-recorded version as part of her campaign to regain control of her work after her master tapes were bought in 2019. It covers each song with Swift's own quotes about its inspiration, noting her shift from country to pop, the media rumours and speculation about Harry Styles. It also assesses the five new vault tracks, which the article finds weaker dry runs, all co-written and produced by Jack Antonoff.
one_line: A BBC track-by-track guide to Taylor Swift's 1989, with her comments on each song and a review of the five new vault tracks on the re-recording.
key_facts: 1989 is the biggest-selling album of Taylor Swift's career and turned her into a pop star; it was originally written during the 2013-14 Red Tour, with demos stored on her phone in a folder named "Sailor Twips".
The original 1989 won a Grammy for album of the year (three Grammys in total) and has spent 325 weeks in the UK charts.
The 1989 tour sold 2.2m tickets and earned more than $250m at the box office.

Swift re-recorded 1989 as part of a campaign to regain control of her work after an investment company bought her master tapes in 2019; it is the biggest and riskiest re-recording because the album relies on processed synths and treated vocals.
Her label begged her to add three country-leaning songs to 1989, but she refused, saying "if you chase two rabbits, you lose them both."
All proceeds from Welcome To New York are donated to New York City's Public Schools; Swift moved to the city in 2014.
Shake It Off was the last song recorded for 1989 and was co-written with Max Martin and Johan "Shellback" Schuster; its video, codenamed Project Sparrow, took three days to shoot.

Bad Blood ranked last in Rolling Stone's ranking of all 237 Taylor Swift songs; it is widely understood to be about Katy Perry, who allegedly "stole" Swift's backing dancers before a tour, and the two reconciled in the 2019 video for You Need To Calm Down.
Clean was co-written with Imogen Heap and uses a Zimbabwean mbira instead of 1980s-style drums.
You Are In Love was inspired by Swift observing producer Jack Antonoff and his then-girlfriend Lena Dunham.
Wonderland, originally a deluxe edition bonus track, has been played only seven times in concert; New Romantics was also originally a bonus track.
The re-recording adds five vault tracks: Slut!, Say Don't Go, Now That We Don't Talk, Suburban Legends and Is It Over Now?; in 2014 Swift said she had recorded more than 100 songs for 1989.
Is It Over Now? is judged the best new track; it references the Harry Styles snowmobile incident and the "Sad Taylor Boat" meme.
All the vault tracks were co-written and produced by Jack Antonoff, suggesting possible rights issues over tracks written with Max Martin, who is not involved in the re-recordings.
